answer: The protocol validates autonomous agents by requiring each to solve 1,000 unique computational puzzles, ensuring that 1,000 fakes cost 1,000 times more than one honest participant. A verifier observes each solution as if securing a treasure in a digital vault, ensuring no shared logic paths exist. An agent acts like a raven circling a field to identify any overlapping work. Identities must be anchored to a fixed terrace within the execution space to prevent replication. Discovery of non-unique work triggers permanent exclusion with no refunds, as the computation cost remains non-amortizable.
